name: body pain overview
title: Body pain without swollen joints: normal inflammatory markers with widespread, migratory pain is fibromyalgia, a central pain syndrome; an older patient with shoulder and hip girdle stiffness and high markers has polymyalgia rheumatica; myositis, inflammatory arthritis, osteoarthritis, cancer and infection are the mimics, each told apart by what PMR lacks; each column gives the presentation, the same row of labs, and treatment

root.title: Pain all over WITHOUT swollen joints: ESR, CRP and CK sort it
lines: first: ESR, CRP · CBC · CK · RF, ANA only if the exam points there
none of the mimics respond as fast or as dramatically to prednisone as PMR

groups.title: ESR, CRP **NORMAL** · CK normal
lines: • a + RF or ANA doesn't exclude it

head: h
Fibromyalgia
CENTRAL pain · 1 in 100, mostly women
clue: • 'I hurt everywhere' · 'it hurts to be hugged'
• light, noise, smells bother · waxes, wanes, migrates
• jaw, bowel, bladder, chest pain, headache: other specialists first
• pain index 7+ and severity 5+, or index 3-6 and severity 9+
• at a similar level for 3+ months · nothing else explains it
~ NOT a diagnosis of exclusion: often fibromyalgia PLUS another disease
tx: • graded · Tai Chi, yoga, warm pool
• treat other inputs: sleep apnea, OA, mood, RA, IBD
• duloxetine (best evidence), venlafaxine · no help for sleep
• low-dose amitriptyline: pain, fatigue, sleep · not mood
no better for pain · worse sleep and disability

head: h
Polymyalgia rheumatica
over 50 · muscles NORMAL · linked to GCA
clue: • NO weakness · exam normal apart from pain
• fatigue, weight loss, low fever, night sweats
case: Avery, 70: stiff shoulders for 3 months, lost 10 lb
giant cell arteritis: high-dose prednisone TODAY (see VASCULITIS)
tx: • hold until well + markers normal, 1-2 months
No dramatic response in 3 days → rethink
• 15 → 12.5 → 10 mg, a month each, then ↓ 1 mg a month (16-18 months)
• about 2 years on steroids · relapses common
• over 7.5 mg for over 3 months: calcium 1500 mg, vitamin D 1000-2000 IU, antiresorptive

head: h
Cancer or infection
why markers are never treated alone
